newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sugar panel to review 1996/97 balance sheet.
newsitem.headline: Sugar panel to review 1996/97 balance sheet.

text.p: The Euroean Union's sugar management committee will review the balance sheet for 1996/97 (July/June) on Wednesday, an EU official said.
"There will be an exchange of information on beet tests in the morning and the figures will be presented to the committee in the afternoon," the official said.
"The committee will discuss production and consumption and the supply balance for 1996/97 before meeting with producers representatives on Thursday," the official added.
The European Commission expects a report to be ready for the committee meeting the following week but the discussions and evaluation will take several weeks more.
The committee will also review the amount of sugar available for export with respect to the GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) ceiling.

"Under the new regulation introduced on July 1 last year the Commmission has the power to reduce quotas, even in the current marketing year, if the GATT limit means that sugar cannot be exported and if it cannot, alternatively, be stored," the official said.
Currently the Commission believes that the amount available for export in 1996/97 will not breach the GATT limit.

"The exercise on Wednesday will have no real impact. The review is being undertaken to ensure that the proceedures are in place should the need to cut quotas ever arise," a European Commission official added.
The committee will continue a review of molasses production and consumption on Wednesday.
"The committee is due to exchange information on market figures dating back to the 1991/92 marketing year as part on an on-going review," the official said.
The committee will also deal with the usual weekly tenders, perodic refunds and molasses duties.
